inspection_summary: Inspected all 912 normalized lines. The source develops a complete semantic bridge from zeta pseudomoments through unitary characteristic-polynomial moments and fixed-margin integer matrices to Ehrhart lattice-point volumes, then proves the bridge by Dirichlet-polynomial diagonalization, cutoff integrals, Euler-product factorization, zeta-pole extraction, and coefficient counting. Formula layout is intermittently degraded by PDF extraction, but the main mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose; exact displayed constants, indices, conjugations, and contour integrands should be scan-verified before formula-level reuse.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and front matter
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the paper's arithmetic-factor times geometric-volume result and its random-unitary interpretation.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta moments and arithmetic/geometric factorization
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Motivates higher-moment asymptotics and separates the conjectural leading coefficient into arithmetic and geometric factors.

sections_inspected.label: Unitary characteristic-polynomial comparison
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents exact unitary moments and the Keating-Snaith correspondence for the geometric zeta-moment factor.

sections_inspected.label: Secular coefficients and fixed-margin matrices
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Connects moments of secular coefficients to counts of nonnegative integer matrices with prescribed margins.

sections_inspected.label: Magic-square enumerators and polytopes
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops polynomiality, reciprocity, generating functions, and Birkhoff-polytope volume for magic-square counts.

sections_inspected.label: Main pseudomoment theorem and random-matrix reformulation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the pseudomoment asymptotic with substochastic-polytope volume and identifies it with truncated characteristic-polynomial moments.

sections_inspected.label: Pseudomagic-square residue representation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Represents lattice points in a dilated polytope by a multivariate contour integral and specializes the constraint matrix to row/column inequalities.

sections_inspected.label: Proof of the main theorem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transforms the analytic moment into diagonal multiplicative data, separates the arithmetic factor, extracts the leading pole term, and recovers the pseudomagic count.

sections_inspected.label: Unequal truncations and symmetry-class generalizations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Extends the count to unequal row/column bounds and sketches symplectic analogues with symmetric matrices and even diagonal constraints.

sections_inspected.label: References and author addresses
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and contact material; no new source-level mathematical mechanism.

accepted_units.title: Higher zeta moments split into arithmetic and geometric factors
accepted_units.why_material: Frames the central problem and the reusable distinction between prime-local arithmetic data and a separate global geometric coefficient in moment asymptotics.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the known second and fourth moments, the higher-moment conjecture, and the Conrey-Ghosh factorization needed to interpret later factors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed exponents and constants are formula-dependent and mildly extraction-fragile; the factorization's semantic role is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Random-unitary characteristic polynomials model the geometric zeta-moment factor
accepted_units.why_material: Gives the paper's first cross-representation bridge: exact Haar-unitary characteristic-polynomial moments yield the conjectured geometric factor for zeta moments.
accepted_units.context_note: Retains the definition of the characteristic polynomial, the exact finite-N moment form, its large-N limit, and the Keating-Snaith conjectural comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The gamma/Barnes-G products are extraction-sensitive, including a likely damaged denominator index; scan verification is required for exact formula reuse.

accepted_units.title: Secular-coefficient moments count fixed-margin nonnegative integer matrices
accepted_units.why_material: Turns random-matrix moments into a discrete transportation-table count, establishing the combinatorial representation later used for pseudomoments.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes secular coefficients, row/column margin notation, examples, and the theorem identifying mixed moments and the equal-margin specialization with magic squares.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mixed-moment display likely loses complex-conjugation typography in extraction; the fixed-margin counting interpretation is prose-supported, but the exact moment formula needs PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Modern magic squares as equal-margin integer matrices
accepted_units.why_material: Separates historical magic squares from the modern enumerative object and illustrates how low-dimensional cases reduce to permutation matrices or a single free parameter.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical discussion supplies terminology; the reusable content is the nonnegative-integer, equal-row-and-column-sum definition and the elementary boundary cases.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The matrix examples and the closed form for H3 are visually laid out and should be scan-checked if their exact entries or coefficients are used.

accepted_units.title: Polynomiality, reciprocity, and palindromic generating functions for magic-square counts
accepted_units.why_material: Packages a counting problem into interchangeable polynomial, negative-evaluation, functional-equation, and rational-generating-function views.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly says the polynomial/zero/functional-equation statements are equivalent to a numerator-symmetry generating-function form.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core claims are readable; exact exponents and example coefficients remain display-dependent and merit scan verification.

accepted_units.title: The leading magic-square coefficient is Birkhoff-polytope volume
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies asymptotic counting growth with the volume of the convex hull of permutation matrices, providing the Ehrhart bridge from discrete counts to geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes both the leading-coefficient statement and the row-stochastic/column-stochastic inequality description of the Birkhoff polytope.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed relative-volume normalization is garbled around lines 325-328; use the prose-level identification unless checked against the retained PDF.

accepted_units.title: Zeta pseudomoments have arithmetic-factor times substochastic-volume leading term
accepted_units.why_material: States the paper's central result: moments of truncated zeta sums have a leading coefficient combining the standard arithmetic factor with the volume of a substochastic matrix polytope.
accepted_units.context_note: The polytope inequalities are included because they define what the geometric factor means rather than merely naming it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theorem display is fragmented by extraction; the leading exponent, error term, and inequality indexing must be scan-verified for exact use, while the prose identifies the geometric factor unambiguously.

accepted_units.title: Truncated characteristic-polynomial moments equal pseudomagic-square counts
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that truncating the random-matrix characteristic polynomial replaces exact magic-square margins by upper-bounded margins, and that the normalized moment limit is the same polytope volume appearing in zeta pseudomoments.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the truncated polynomial, the finite count G_k(l), its lattice-polytope interpretation, polynomial growth, and the random-matrix limit for the volume.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and set description recover the mechanism; exact powers and the sample G2 polynomial are formula-dependent.

accepted_units.title: Multivariate residues count lattice points in the pseudomagic polytope
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a general conversion from linear inequalities for a lattice polytope to a multivariate generating-function contour integral, then specializes it to row and column capacity constraints.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the general Ax<=b setup, the dilation count L(P,l), the column-vector generating-function rule, and the specialized 2k by k^2 constraint matrix.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The contour integrals and block matrix are heavily layout-dependent; the surrounding prose preserves the construction, but exact integrands and contour factors require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Mean-value diagonalization converts the pseudomoment to a constrained multiplicative sum
accepted_units.why_material: Uses the Dirichlet-polynomial mean-value theorem to replace an analytic time average by a sum over two k-tuples constrained to have equal products.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the restricted divisor-count definition and the expanded equality-of-products form that becomes Euler-factorizable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The equality constraint is clear in prose/display, but radicals, powers, and summation bounds are extraction-fragile.

accepted_units.title: Cutoff integrals encode the truncation bounds as a multiple contour integral
accepted_units.why_material: Introduces a discontinuous Perron-type integral and applies one copy per variable, turning finite cutoff conditions into complex parameters attached to the multiplicative sum.
accepted_units.context_note: The unit ends after the definition of the multivariable Dirichlet series F and notation needed for its factorization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This step depends on exact contour conventions and exponents whose display extraction is fragmented; reuse should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The constrained Dirichlet series factors into zeta poles times a regular Euler product
accepted_units.why_material: Separates universal singular factors indexed by pairs of variables from an absolutely convergent Euler product whose value at the origin is the arithmetic factor a_k.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the analytic counterpart of separating geometry from arithmetic in the initial moment conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The factorization is explicit but line-broken; convergence region, local exponents, and the specialization defining a_k need formula-level scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Zeta-pole replacement isolates the leading geometric contour integral
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why only the polar parts of the zeta factors and the origin value of the regular Euler product control the leading term, pulling out the arithmetic factor.
accepted_units.context_note: Connects the exact multiple-integral expression to its leading asymptotic without yet identifying the remaining integral combinatorially.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual pole-extraction step is prose-supported; the exact integral and error control are formula-dependent and abbreviated as standard bounds.

accepted_units.title: Geometric contour coefficients recover pseudomagic matrices
accepted_units.why_material: Expands each geometric denominator, groups monomials by row and column sums, and uses the cutoff integral to show that the residual leading integral equals the pseudomagic-square count G_k(log X).
accepted_units.context_note: This closes the proof by identifying coefficient choices with nonnegative integer matrices satisfying row and column upper bounds.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The matrix-coefficient semantics are explicit in prose; exact exponential signs, contour normalizations, and bound notation should be scan-verified.

accepted_units.title: The direct equality of the two contour integrals remains elusive
accepted_units.why_material: Records a genuine method limitation: the lattice-point residue integral motivated the proof, but the authors could not directly transform it into the analytic integral and instead proved equality through the shared count.
accepted_units.context_note: Useful as a distinction between motivational representation and operative proof route.

accepted_units.title: Unequal truncations produce anisotropic pseudomagic bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the same proof mechanism survives unequal cutoff scales, replacing a single dilation parameter by row- and column-specific logarithmic bounds.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the bounded-ratio scaling assumption and the generalized integer-matrix count G_k(l1,...,lk).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The generalized count is recoverable, but the product-moment display and assignment of row versus column bounds are visually fragile and require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Symplectic secular moments impose symmetry and even-diagonal constraints
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates how changing random-matrix symmetry class changes the associated combinatorial objects from arbitrary transportation tables to symmetric tables with parity constraints, equivalently regular multigraphs with loops.
accepted_units.context_note: Supplies a structural comparison rather than only announcing that an analogue exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose constraints are clear; the precise stability bound and moment exponent in the theorem display need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Symplectic-family pseudomoments are governed by constrained symmetric-matrix counts
accepted_units.why_material: Carries the arithmetic/geometric mechanism to quadratic-character L-functions and links the leading polynomial to truncated symplectic characteristic-polynomial moments and Ehrhart growth.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the arithmetic factor, the family pseudomoment statement, the definition of F_k(l), and its random-matrix interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The exact Euler product, family averaging normalization, constants, and error exponent are extraction-fragile; the symmetric-count bridge is prose-supported.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Arithmetic data times geometric capacity volume
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The leading pseudomoment coefficient separates because prime-local multiplicativity becomes a regular Euler-product value, while the coupled cutoff constraints become the volume-growth coefficient of a substochastic matrix polytope.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Established here for fixed integer moments of the stated truncated sums; exact constants and lower-order control are formula-sensitive and no universality beyond the treated setup is proved.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One transportation-table object links random matrices and zeta pseudomoments
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Secular-coefficient expansion and Dirichlet-series coefficient expansion independently produce nonnegative integer matrices indexed by paired factors; truncation changes prescribed margins into upper-bounded margins.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a source-internal structural identification, not evidence that all zeta statistics are modeled by unitary matrices.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Ehrhart theory converts exact finite counts into asymptotic geometric constants
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Polynomial lattice-point enumeration makes polytope volume simultaneously the leading growth coefficient of pseudomagic counts and the normalized limit of truncated characteristic-polynomial moments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Relative-volume normalization and some displayed formulas are extraction-damaged and must be checked before numerical use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Proof architecture as successive representation changes
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Time averaging enforces multiplicative diagonal equality, contour cutoffs expose complex parameters, Euler products isolate arithmetic poles, and geometric-series coefficients turn the remaining analytic object into constrained matrices.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source invokes standard zeta bounds for the leading-term passage and does not spell out every analytic error estimate in this extracted text.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Random-matrix truncation explains substochastic rather than stochastic geometry
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Full characteristic-polynomial moments correspond to exact-margin magic squares and the Birkhoff polytope, whereas truncation relaxes exact margins to capacities and replaces it by the substochastic polytope.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The comparison concerns the moment/count identities presented here and should not be promoted to a general equivalence of the underlying probabilistic models.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry class is encoded as combinatorial constraints
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Moving from unitary to symplectic matrices changes unrestricted margin tables into symmetric nonnegative matrices with even diagonal, and the analogous L-function pseudomoment inherits that constrained count.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The orthogonal case is only mentioned, and the symplectic L-function result is stated without the full proof in this source.
